title: Option to render MetricRange transitions as a rectangle instead of an interpolated shape

complexity.rationale: A repo-wide search for `interpolate` across vega-spec-builder/src turns up zero usages on any mark — no Area or Line mark in this codebase configures Vega's `interpolate` field today, so there is no existing pattern to copy for the new option; it is genuinely new, unprecedented logic at its single site (getAreaMark). One open design decision also remains (which Vega interpolate value, and whether it should be a boolean toggle or a full enum). One real site + one open decision => 3, not higher, since the change itself (adding one conditional encode field) is small and scoped to a single mark builder function.

summary: MetricRange is a Line child (MetricRangeParentOptions = LineSpecOptions in metricRangeUtils.ts:31) whose range is rendered by getAreaMark (packages/vega-spec-builder/src/area/areaUtils.ts:71-114). That function never sets Vega's `interpolate` field on the area mark, so it renders with Vega's AreaMark default ('linear'), independently interpolating the metricStart and metricEnd boundary fields between points; when adjacent points' ranges cross through zero this produces a diamond/rhombus shape instead of the rectangle the reporter wants for 'this range started here and ended here' semantics. There is currently no prop to opt into a step-style render, so this is a missing feature, not a regression in existing behavior.
requirements: Add a new option to MetricRangeOptions (packages/vega-spec-builder/src/types/marks/supplemental/metricRangeSpec.types.ts) controlling the range area's interpolation — e.g. `interpolate?: 'linear' | 'step-after'` (or a simpler boolean such as `smoothTransitions?: boolean`, defaulting to true/current behavior).

Thread the resolved value through AreaMarkOptions (packages/vega-spec-builder/src/area/areaUtils.ts:44-69) and set Vega's `interpolate` on the returned AreaMark in getAreaMark (currently entirely unset, lines 89-113).

Apply the same resolved value to the paired metric line mark built in getMetricRangeMark (packages/vega-spec-builder/src/metricRange/metricRangeUtils.ts:185-231) so the line and its range stay visually consistent across the same transition.

Determine which Vega interpolate value best matches 'started here, ended here' — most likely 'step-after' so the range holds its value until the next data point rather than stepping early — and document the choice.
Default to current ('linear') behavior so existing MetricRange usages are visually unaffected; the new mode must be opt-in.

edgeCases.case: Only one metric range point (no adjacent segment to interpolate across)
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: No visible difference between modes — interpolation only affects rendering between two or more points.

edgeCases.case: Metric range with metricStart === metricEnd for every point
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: Renders as a degenerate flat line regardless of interpolate mode; not specific to this feature.
The chosen interpolate mode applies identically whether the range is always visible or only shown on hover, since it's set on the same area mark either way.
Same option, default, and resolved Vega interpolate value in vega-spec-builder-s2/src/metricRange and area/areaUtils.ts, which have the identical current gap.

crossCutting.notes: requiresS1S2Parity: vega-spec-builder-s2/src/area/areaUtils.ts and vega-spec-builder-s2/src/metricRange/metricRangeUtils.ts mirror the s1 files exactly and have the identical missing-interpolate gap (confirmed via grep — no `interpolate` usage in either package).

implementationPlan.change: Add the new interpolate/smoothTransitions option to MetricRangeOptions, with a runtime default preserving current behavior.
Add an `interpolate` field to AreaMarkOptions and set it on the AreaMark returned from getAreaMark.
Thread the new option from MetricRangeSpecOptions into AreaMarkOptions (and the paired LineMarkOptions) in getMetricRangeMark.
Expose the new prop at the React boundary.
Thread through the default value for the new prop.
Mirror the new option for S2 parity.
Mirror the interpolate field addition for S2 parity.
Mirror the option threading for S2 parity.
Add a story demonstrating the new mode across a zero-to-X transition, following existing story ordering/grouping.

openQuestions: Should the new option be a simple boolean (e.g. smoothTransitions / disableSmoothTransitions) or expose the full Vega interpolate enum for future flexibility?
Should 'step-after' become the new default for MetricRange going forward (a breaking visual change) or remain strictly opt-in?
